carousel.missionText: CAPEC's mission is to provide in-depth economic analyses to inform public policy decisions in Côte d'Ivoire. We work to strengthen the capacities of national stakeholders in economic management, strategic planning, and the implementation of reforms. At the same time, we promote applied research and innovation to foster inclusive and sustainable growth that addresses local economic challenges.

news1.title: Inaugural Lecture on the Occasion of CAPEC's 30th Anniversary
news1.excerpt: CAPEC celebrated its 30th anniversary on October 8 and 9, 2024, in Abidjan, in the presence of Mr. Emmanuel Ahoutou KOFFI, Minister and Director of Cabinet of the Vice-President, who delivered a remarkable inaugural lecture. He praised CAPEC's impact on public policy in Côte d'Ivoire and within the UEMOA-ECOWAS region, while encouraging the institution to innovate in response to climate, technological, and industrial challenges. This anniversary provided an opportunity to review three decades of expertise and outline prospects for inclusive and sustainable development.

motDuDirecteur.title: Director's Message
motDuDirecteur.paragraph1: It is with great pleasure that I welcome you to the official website of the Policy Analysis Unit for Economic Policies at CIRES (CAPEC). This digital space is intended to be a dynamic showcase of our institution — a place for sharing information and dialogue in support of applied economic research and public policy decision-making.
motDuDirecteur.paragraph2: Since its creation in 1993, CAPEC has positioned itself as a major player in policy analysis in Côte d'Ivoire and Africa. Our mission is to produce rigorous analyses based on reliable, evidence-based data to inform the strategic choices of public decision-makers, private-sector actors, civil society, development partners and all stakeholders involved in economic and social development. It serves as a bridge between academia and development actors.
motDuDirecteur.paragraph3: Our renewed website has been designed to meet your needs and is now the preferred channel to keep you updated daily on our achievements. Through this site, we invite you to explore our research work, publications, ongoing projects, analytical tools, as well as our training and knowledge dissemination activities. Please visit our website regularly to access up-to-date information about our activities.
motDuDirecteur.paragraph4: We firmly believe that shared knowledge is a powerful lever for transformation. For this reason, CAPEC is committed to remaining accessible, open and attentive to society’s needs.
motDuDirecteur.closing: Happy browsing to all, and thank you for your interest in our work.

1.title: Director of CAPEC
1.bio:
Alban A. E. Ahouré is a Full Professor of Economics at Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny in Abidjan (since 2021) and Director of the Policy Analysis Unit for Economic Policies at CIRES (CAPEC) since 2011. He earned his PhD in Economics from Kobe University (Japan, 2006) and specializes in applied microeconomics, labor economics and human resources, institutional economics, game theory and policy evaluation.

He has coordinated numerous studies on competitiveness, taxation, the private sector, informality, agriculture, governance and development prospects for national, regional (WAEMU, ECOWAS) and international institutions (AfDB, World Bank, UNDP, WFP, FAO, UNICEF, etc.).

Author of several books and peer-reviewed articles, his research focuses on employability, economic inclusion, inclusive business models and structural transformation in Africa.

Elected in 2024 as an Honorary Member of the Royal European Academy of Doctors (RAED) and featured repeatedly in the Who's Who in Côte d'Ivoire, he actively contributes to scientific debate and development policy in Africa.

3.title: Researcher - Head of Administrative Management
3.bio: KRAMO Kouakou Germain holds a PhD in Economics. He is a researcher at the Policy Analysis Unit for Economic Policies at CIRES (CAPEC) where he has coordinated or contributed to several projects and studies on the Ivorian economy and other African countries. With around ten years of research experience, Dr KRAMO is Head of Administrative Management at CAPEC and an Assistant Professor at the Faculty of Economics and Management at Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny. His research interests include public finance, international trade, economic integration, intellectual property rights and productivity.

4.title: Researcher at the Economic Policy Analysis Unit (CAPEC)
4.bio: BECHO Isabelle (née N'DRI) is an economist holding a PhD in Economics from Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny (Cocody) and a microprogram diploma in Applied Development Economics from Université Laval. She is a teacher-researcher at the Virtual University of Côte d'Ivoire (UVCI) and a researcher at CAPEC. Her expertise includes impact evaluation of public policies, poverty analysis, vulnerability assessment, political economy and governance, gender analysis, firm analysis, informal sector analysis, inclusive finance, microfinance, development economics, quantitative and qualitative methodologies and data analysis. She has worked on gender, vulnerability and violent extremism projects, collaborated with UN Women, and led research with USAID on COVID-19 policy impacts on women and youth in West Africa. She has also consulted for Equal Access on projects to reduce violent extremism through economic and social inclusion of youth. She teaches microeconomics, data analysis and research methods to students and public/private professionals and is member of scientific associations such as the International Association of Francophone Microfinance Researchers (AICFM) and the Association of Women Researchers of Côte d'Ivoire (AFEMCI).

5.title: Environmental Economist & Senior Researcher at CAPEC
5.bio: Mr. BEKE Tite Ehuitché is an Associate Professor at the Faculty of Economics and Management, Université FHB (Abidjan). He holds a PhD in Environmental Economics and is a Senior Researcher at CAPEC. His publications and study reports focus on resilient agricultural value chains in the face of climate change, food security, the green economy, just ecological transition and green jobs. He is a member of the operational GJAM (Green Jobs Assessment Model) team and Team21 Côte d’Ivoire.

6.title: Economist Researcher at CAPEC
6.bio: Dr TRAORE Nohoua holds a PhD in Development Economics from Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny and a professional postgraduate diploma in Project Management. He is currently an Assistant Professor at Université Alassane Ouattara and an economist researcher at the CAPEC. Dr Traoré has contributed to several international research projects funded by IDRC focusing on firm performance in francophone Sub-Saharan Africa, economic inclusion of youth and women, inclusive entrepreneurship and COVID-19 impacts. His national contributions include work on informal sector supervision, tobacco product taxation, entrepreneur status, tax optimization and exemptions, privatization, and private sector competitiveness. He has also trained fiscal administration staff across francophone Africa on research methods applied to taxation for the African Tax Administration Forum (ATAF). He publishes in international journals and is a member of scientific committees including the African Tax Research Network and Sustainability, Research & Innovation Network.

7.title: Researcher and Development Economist at CAPEC
7.bio: Holder of a PhD in Economics from ENSEA (Abidjan), with strong training in statistics and mathematics, he is a development economist and researcher at CAPEC, responsible for data management. His combined expertise enables rigorous applied economic research. His work focuses on financial stability, public debt, structural transformation and policy evaluation using advanced econometric methods to provide robust, decision-oriented analyses.

8.title: Researcher at the Economic Policy Analysis Unit (CAPEC)
8.bio: Dr KOUADIO holds a PhD in Economics from Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny (Cocody). As a teacher-researcher and consultant, he has conducted numerous studies for international and local institutions. At CAPEC he contributed to many research projects, progressing from research assistant to associate researcher. He is a member of AfricaLics and his research interests include development economics, innovation management, firm economics, knowledge economy, digital economy, transport economics and quantitative techniques (statistics and econometrics).

9.title: Macroeconomist Researcher at CAPEC
9.bio: Kacou Yves Thierry Kacou holds a PhD in Economics from the University of Ulsan (South Korea). He is a lecturer-researcher at INPHB (Yamoussoukro) and a macroeconomist researcher at CAPEC. He has contributed to studies on fiscal policy, economic modelling and forward-looking analysis, including development of a multi-sector DSGE model for the Ivorian economy and analysis of macroeconomic consequences of infrastructure delays and climate risk adaptation in WAEMU countries. His interests include public policy impact, applied econometrics and macroeconomic modelling.

11.title: Macroeconomist Researcher at CAPEC
11.bio: Touré Talnan Aboulaye has been a lecturer-researcher in economics at INP-HB (Yamoussoukro) since September 2023 and a junior macroeconomist researcher at CAPEC. He has contributed to studies on the competitiveness challenges of the Ivorian economy, the impact of electricity price increases (policy brief), the national strategy for resource mobilization (SNRMT), socio-economic impact assessment of tax exemptions, and the evaluation of fiscal measures such as changes in corporate tax regimes (BIC). He holds a PhD in Economics from Kobe University (Japan) and his research interests include monetary, banking and financial economics and fiscal policy.
